actualMethod: open one official read handle; handle.read(0, undefined); derive closers with the installed interruptedTurnClosers over THAT array; classify each event by its position in the resulting array

syntheticRecoveryCounts.h1-interrupted: >0 (exact closers depend on the open step)

forkInheritance: a supported buildForkSeed child: inheritedEventCount=2, isSeeded=true, parentSession recorded, inherited seqs 0..1 marked inherited, forked closers at seq>=2 NOT inherited and carrying the forked cause
concurrentMutationControl: test S4 appends to the same session AFTER the first read; the first page is unchanged (persistedEventCount stays 2 and its synthetic seq set is identical), and a fresh read observes the new balanced state (persistedEventCount 4, 0 synthetic)
errorBehaviour: SESSION_MISSING for an absent session; a corrupted artifact yields a non-READ_OK state with zero events and a null known count, never an empty success; close() is idempotent
readOnlyVerification: sha256+size of the session artifact is identical before and after the diagnostic reads (S1, S7)
resourceCleanup: each read opens and closes its own handle; close() disposes the Cordis fiber; five sequential reads leave the source unchanged (S7)
invariant: every storedEvents entry is classified from the persistence read that produced it; every event from interruptedTurnClosers is synthetic; no later independent storage count determines the boundary
verdict: PASS — one-read derivation established and measured byte-parity with the official cold read
limitations: Node v24.14.1 is below the repository-declared engines minimum of >=24.15.0; the runtime acceptance result is qualified accordingly
